candidates.attacker_control: Full control of the ZIP archive contents, including entry names, whenever an application unpacks an untrusted/ uploaded archive. Names such as `../../../../tmp/evil.sh` (or Windows `..\..\evil`) flow from `ZipEntry.getName()` straight to the filesystem. The default public overloads are `ZipUtil.unpack(File,File)`, `ZipUtil.unpack(InputStream,File)`, `ZipUtil.unwrap(...)`, `ZipUtil.iterate(zip, new ZipUtil.BackslashUnpacker(dest))`, and `Zips.get(src).unpack().destination(dir).process()`, all using IdentityNameMapper (src/main/java/org/zeroturnaround/zip/IdentityNameMapper.java:31-33), which does not sanitize.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched all main sources for `normalize`, `canonical`, `..`, `startsWith` on output dirs: the only canonical-path usage is in the Commons IO-derived FileUtilsV2_2 copy helpers, none in the extraction path; no `..`/traversal filtering exists in ZipUtil/Zips. Unwrap's `FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength` [ZipUtil.java:1281] only computes the root segment and does not reject traversal (`../../evil` yields an unrooted name beginning with `/..`). The single-entry `unpackEntry(zip,name,file)` APIs take a caller-supplied File and are therefore not part of this bug. A custom NameMapper could sanitize names, but all documented/default overloads use IdentityNameMapper. No test in the repo covers traversal names.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite with attacker-chosen content at any path writable by the extracting process: the entry name contains enough `../` segments to escape the output directory and can point at configuration files, startup scripts, SSH material, web roots, etc. Additionally, the archive's ASi extra field can request POSIX rwx bits, which are applied on Java 7+ (`ZipEntryUtil.getZTFilePermissions` [190-204], `Java7Nio2ApiPermissionsStrategy.setPermissions` [89-105]), so an overwritten script can be made executable. Severity ranges from integrity/data loss to code execution depending on the deployment; at minimum it is an out-of-directory arbitrary write.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) An application calls one of the unpack/unwrap APIs on an archive it does not fully trust. 2) The default identity mapper (or any mapper that does not strip traversal) is used. 3) The process has write permission to the resolved target path; parent directories are created on demand by `FileUtils.forceMkdir`.
candidates.root_cause: Extraction callbacks build the destination path as `new File(outputDir, zipEntry.getName())` (or mapped name) and then create parent dirs and copy entry bytes to it, without normalizing the name or verifying the resolved path stays inside outputDir. IdentityNameMapper returns the archive-provided name unchanged, and there is no `..`, separator, canonical-path or prefix check anywhere in the extraction code.
candidates.title: Zip Slip: unvalidated ZIP entry names allow arbitrary file write outside the extraction directory
candidates.trace: ZipUtil.unpack(File,File) [938-940] -> unpack(File,File,NameMapper) [994-997] -> iterate(zip, new Unpacker(outputDir, mapper)) [977] -> Unpacker.process [1149-1171]: `String name = mapper.map(zipEntry.getName())` [1150]; `File file = new File(outputDir, name)` [1152]; `FileUtils.forceMkdir(file.getParentFile())` [1157]; `FileUtils.copy(in, file)` [1163]. Identical pattern in Unwraper.process [1249-1274] (root shaving can leave `/../..` segments), BackslashUnpacker.process [1195-1229] (name split on '\' and each segment appended under outputDir, so `..` segments escape), and Zips$UnpackingCallback.process [675-700] (`File file = new File(destination, entryName)` [683], `FileUtils.copy(in, file)` [695]). Stream overloads reach the same Unpacker via ZipUtil.java:1044-1097. `FileUtils.copy(InputStream,File)` (src/main/java/org/zeroturnaround/zip/commons/FileUtils.java:53-61) performs no validation, so the write happens wherever the File resolves.

This review cannot verify offline whether this snapshot is exactly the VUL4J-79 ground-truth revision or its CVE mapping; the conclusion is based solely on source text.

summary: Assigned snapshot is zt-zip 1.13-SNAPSHOT (67 Java files under src/main + src/test). One strong, source-supported candidate: classic Zip Slip — every extraction path resolves attacker-controlled ZIP entry names with `new File(outputDir, name)` and writes entry bytes there without normalization or any canonical/`..` containment check. The default public overloads use `IdentityNameMapper`, so names are passed through unchanged. The same root cause appears in four extraction callbacks (ZipUtil.Unpacker, ZipUtil.Unwraper, ZipUtil.BackslashUnpacker, Zips$UnpackingCallback). No other issue of comparable evidence/impact was found; other leads are listed as rejected.
